title: The Brahmagupta-Fibonacci identity over the constructed integers
statement: For all integers a, b, c, d the product of two sums of two squares is again a sum of two squares: (a^2+b^2)(c^2+d^2) = (ac-bd)^2 + (ad+bc)^2. The conjugate grouping (ac+bd)^2 + (ad-bc)^2 is a SEPARATE declaration (Int.brahmaguptaFibonacci'), not a corollary of this one: the two are different statements about the same product, and Fermat's descent needs specifically the conjugate, because with c = a and d = b modulo m that grouping's cross terms are ac+bd = a^2+b^2 = 0 and ad-bc = ab-ba = 0, so BOTH are divisible by m, while this grouping's are not.

formal.statement: theorem Int.brahmaguptaFibonacci : ((x0 : Int) -> ((x1 : Int) -> ((x2 : Int) -> ((x3 : Int) -> Eq.{1} Int (Int.mul (Int.add (Int.mul x0 x0) (Int.mul x1 x1)) (Int.add (Int.mul x2 x2) (Int.mul x3 x3))) (Int.add (Int.mul (Int.sub (Int.mul x0 x2) (Int.mul x1 x3)) (Int.sub (Int.mul x0 x2) (Int.mul x1 x3))) (Int.mul (Int.add (Int.mul x0 x3) (Int.mul x1 x2)) (Int.add (Int.mul x0 x3) (Int.mul x1 x2))))))))

evidence.notes: Two independent failure modes, so the exit status depends on the finding rather than on the run completing: int_theorem_inventory exits non-zero when the named filter matches nothing, and grep -c exits 1 printing 0 when the anchored line is absent. Anchored with [[:space:]] and never with a backslash-t, which a scripted (GNU) grep reads as a literal t. grep -c rather than grep -q, which would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail. --release is MANDATORY: this tool builds the constructed carriers and overflows the default debug thread stack. The anchor AFTER the name is load-bearing here, because Int.brahmaguptaFibonacci' is a different declaration whose rendered name has Int.brahmaguptaFibonacci as a prefix.

notes: The proof term was NOT authored. ring::int::declare (ADR-1582, under ADR-0601's producer discipline) parsed the goal, normalised both sides to a signed sum of monomials and emitted a term the kernel then re-checked; the module carries no mul_comm/left_distrib chain for this statement at all. MEASURED SIDE FINDING, recorded here because it cost this lane a build: the same producer DECLINES any goal whose normal form collapses to zero. add 0 a normalises to the item list [Mono[a], Num(0)] and a to [Mono[a]]; the trailing zero numeral is not dropped, the lists compare unequal, and the search reports NotAnIdentity. Int.zero_add, Int.sub_self, Int.add_sub_cancel_right and Int.mul_sub_mul_comm are hand-proved in the same module for exactly that reason. THE CONCRETE TEST CANNOT SEE AN OPERAND SWAP: (ac-bd)^2 and (bd-ac)^2 are equal at every argument, so a mutation transposing the subtraction is still a TRUE theorem; only the_two_identities_state_the_intended_groupings, which runs at free variables, separates them.
